connect.scopeHint: Leave empty for the whole server
connect.scopeMissing: That channel does not exist on this server.

channels.title: Channels
channels.whisper: Hold to whisper to this channel
channels.listen: Hold to also listen to this channel

tx.title: Transmit
tx.noProcessing: No processing: no noise suppression, AGC, echo cancellation or limiting.
tx.continuousNoKey: Always on never keys the station's radio (it would stay on the air). Use push to talk or VOX to transmit through the station.
tx.stereoTestHint: Sends a stereo white-noise test (both / left / right, about 40 s) to the channel so the other position can check channel separation. It replaces your input while it plays and never keys the station's radio. Needs Stereo on in Link.

link.title: Link
link.clamped: Limited by the server's bandwidth cap

settings.title: Settings
settings.reconnect: Server and PTT hardware changes apply on the next connect.
settings.stationVox: Key the rig on incoming audio (VOX)
settings.muteHome: Mute my channel while listening in
settings.hotkeyHint: Use a modifier (Ctrl, Alt, Shift) or a function key.
settings.otrspPort: OTRSP serial port (logger on this computer)
settings.otrspHelp: Set this only on the computer where the logger runs; the other position follows over the server (stereo servers only). TX1/TX2 select the transmitting radio, RX1/RX2 the radio heard, stereo receive selects both. Use a virtual serial port pair (for example com0com) between the logger and this program.
settings.roleOperatorHint: You hear radio 1 on the left and radio 2 on the right; choose radio 1, radio 2 or both. Your voice is sent to the radio selected at the station.
settings.roleStationHint: Send radio 1 as left and radio 2 as right. The operator's voice and PTT go to the transmitting radio only.
settings.singleDevice: Both radios on one stereo sound card (radio 1 left, radio 2 right)
settings.station2Hint: Radio 2 can share radio 1's port on the other line (for example RTS for radio 1, DTR for radio 2). Timing settings are shared with radio 1.
settings.keyerUdp: Send OTRSP to the CW keyer on this computer (UDP)
settings.keyerUdpHint: Sends TX1/TX2 (and the RX state) to 127.0.0.1 on every change and every 2 seconds, so the keyer keys the transmitting radio. Works wherever the logger runs, and also when not connected.
settings.devicesLive: A new sound device is used at once: while connected, the connection restarts for a moment.

routing.title: Two radios
routing.otrspHint: No logger is sending OTRSP: choose a port in Settings, or let the other position's logger drive it

servers.title: Servers
servers.empty: The list is empty. Add a server to connect.
servers.name: Server name
servers.errDuplicate: Another server already has this name.
servers.errHost: Enter an IP address or DNS name, without spaces.
servers.settingsHint: Changes to the server you are connected to apply the next time you connect.

cat.notRunning: Station PTT is not running: tick Enabled above, then disconnect and connect again.
cat.notRunningOffline: Station PTT runs while connected. Connect to see the radio's state here.
cat.notTransmitting: The radio has not gone into transmit. It may be ignoring the TX; command on this connection: try the serial port, or the network with no password (plain CAT on port 9200).

k4.title: Elecraft K4 CAT, radio {{radio}}
k4.serialHint: 38400 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.
k4.networkHint: With a password, this connects as K4 Remote (port 9205). Leave the password empty to send plain CAT text to the port you enter.
k4.testHint: Test reads the radio's ID and does not transmit. Disconnect first if this program is already using the radio's port.
k4.keyTestHint: Sends TX; to the radio, holds it for 2 seconds, then RX;. The radio really transmits: use a dummy load or the radio's TX TEST mode. Disconnect first.
k4.keyNoTx: The radio did NOT report transmit.
